subject: URGENT: 429 cascade following org cutover - mitigation & exec brief
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena@medstream.health>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: platform-ops@medstream.health
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 22:14:00 -0000
Subject: Production spike: 429s after org cutover - urgent

Michael —

We just completed the org->project mapping cutover you coordinated, and within ~10 minutes we saw a cascade of 429s across several endpoints. Customer-facing errors started showing up at 22:05 UTC and we observed ~18% of requests failing with 429 and many of the rest returning timeouts. Our clients are seeing repeat retries which amplified the load; this is impacting our clinical workloads (time-sensitive).

Attached: server_logs_20260918.zip (filtered log bundle), client_retry_trace.txt

We need an immediate mitigation (temporary quota bump or route to fallback) and a write-up of root cause. Please escalate — this is high priority for MedStream Health.

—Elena
Elena Soto
VP, Platform Engineering
MedStream Health

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@medstream.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 02:07:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Production spike: 429s after org cutover - urgent

Elena —

Thanks for the quick heads-up and the logs. I'm escalating this immediately. Preliminary read: the 429 pattern looks like an org->tier mapping that assigned several high-throughput projects to a lower quota band during the cutover; clients then retried aggressively which created a feedback loop.

Immediate actions I am initiating now:
- Asking infra to temporarily raise the project-level token quota for the affected projects by 3x (15m window to stabilize).
- Requesting a short client-side retry backoff from MedStream (can you confirm you can flip a config?)
- Looping in our SRE (Rishi) for live throttling analysis and to prepare a hotfix to prevent incorrect tier assignment on cutover.

Marissa / Grace — can you prepare an exec note and ownership for credit/communications? I'll pull logs and a timeline and will follow with a proposed rollback if needed.

Michael Grant
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena@medstream.health>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 04:22:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Production spike: 429s after org cutover - urgent

Team — quick update from SRE side (live):

Observations:
- Correlated 10:05–10:20 UTC: sharp increase in 429s tied to token bucket exhaustion at project scope.
- Origin: a config diff in the migration script that defaulted new projects to the "standard" quota band instead of "enterprise" when org->project mappings were applied.
- Client retry policy (exponential with low jitter) is compounding the load; we see retry loops in the client traces.

Immediate mitigations applied (19 Sep 04:05 UTC):
1) Temporary quota bump applied to the three affected projects (IDs: proj-1174, proj-1175, proj-1180).
2) Traffic routed away from the overloaded GPU pool to a warm fallback pool for low-latency inference (adds ~50ms p95).
3) Hot patch queued: reject new mappings that do not include explicit tier annotations (MR 452).

Next steps:
- Postmortem timeline and RCA to follow.
- Grace/Marissa: recommend offering a one-time usage credit and a joint customer call with SRE and Solutions.

Rishi Malhotra
SRE Lead, Inference Runtime

From: Elena Soto <elena@medstream.health>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: platform-ops@medstream.health, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 08:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Production spike: 429s after org cutover - urgent

Thanks — we pushed a temporary client backoff at 07:55 UTC (added jitter + increased base delay) which helped level the load. We confirm the temporary quotas and the routing change reduced 429s to under 1% by 07:58 UTC; however a subset of long-running jobs experienced timeouts and we have partially degraded functionality for a critical clinical pipeline.

MedStream needs two things from Redwood ASAP:
1) A short executive brief that we can share with our board/ops stakeholders explaining the root cause and the timeline for permanent remediation.
2) Compensation for the incident window — this is material given our SLA and the downstream clinical impact.

We'll stand by for the postmortem and the PR reference. Appreciate the quick response.

—Elena

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@medstream.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -0000
Subject: Post-incident summary & action items — MedStream 429 surge (DL-7832)

Elena / team —

Short summary (TL;DR):
- Incident: spike of 429s and timeouts during org->project mapping cutover (2026-09-18 22:05 UTC).
- Root cause: migration script defaulted projects to an incorrect quota band causing effective quota undersizing for enterprise workloads; client retry behavior generated a retry storm.
- Immediate mitigation: temporary quota bumps, traffic reroute to fallback pool, client backoff applied by MedStream. System stabilized within ~10 minutes of mitigations.

Impact:
- Duration: ~22:05–22:15 UTC (peak), residual client errors reported until 22:30 UTC.
- Affected projects: proj-1174, proj-1175, proj-1180.
- Business impact: degraded throughput for a small set of critical jobs; customer-reported disruptions to a clinical ingestion pipeline.

Action items (owners/timeframes):
1) Permanent fix to migration script to require explicit tier annotation (Rishi) — MR 452 under review; deploy to prod by 2026-09-23.
2) Add validation checks to cutover workflow to detect quota mismatch before applying (SRE + Platform) — owner Rishi, due 2026-09-24.
3) Add automatic short-term grace quotas for enterprise accounts during cutovers (Platform Product) — owner Michael Grant, proposal by 2026-09-22.
4) Customer remediation: one-time usage credit and joint post-incident review call (Sales/CS) — owner Marissa Cole, propose credit and schedule by 2026-09-21.
5) Improve monitoring: create a synthetic check that verifies expected p50/p95 token consumption per project after mapping changes — owner Grace O'Connor, 2026-09-25.

We'll prepare a concise exec brief for your stakeholders and a timeline for remediation. Marissa will follow up on compensation. Please let us know any additional concerns; we take this seriously and will prioritize completion of the action items.

Michael Grant
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: server_logs_20260918.zip, client_retry_trace.txt
Reference: PR: https://git.redwoodinference.com/runtimes/patches/merge_requests/452
